topic: The Engine of Intelligence: Understanding Cost Functions and Gradient Descent

sections.title: Introduction: The 'Error' Concept
lecture_lines: The cost function measures neural network error.
It calculates the difference between prediction and truth.
A wrong guess equals a high cost.
animations: Show a target point representing perfect model accuracy.
Show model predictions failing to reach the target point.
Define 'error' as the gap between prediction and target.
Highlight the gap in #FF0000 to emphasize magnitude.

sections.title: Visualizing the Cost Surface
lecture_lines: Visualize the cost function as a landscape.
Low valleys represent high model accuracy.
We want the network to reach the valley.
The goal is minimizing the cost.
animations: Draw a 3D cost landscape surface in #00FFFF.
Place a ball at the top of the landscape.
Show the ball rolling towards the lowest point.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Gradient Descent
lecture_lines: Gradient descent guides the network downhill.
The gradient shows the direction of steepest slope.
We move in the negative direction of the gradient.
Weights update incrementally with each step.
Small steps help navigate toward the minimum.
animations: Display the loss function formula in #FFFF00.
Indicate the local slope with a tangent line in #FF00FF.
Animate the point shifting down the slope incrementally.
Draw vector showing direction of steepest descent.
Update the loss function value in real-time.

sections.title: Hyperparameters: Step Size and Learning Rate
lecture_lines: Learning rate determines the step size.
Large steps might overshoot the valley.
Tiny steps make learning agonizingly slow.
animations: Visualize a step size vector in #00FF00.
Demonstrate small steps converging smoothly to the minimum.
Demonstrate large steps overshooting the minimum point.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Iterative Loop
lecture_lines: The process repeats in an iterative loop.
Forward pass calculates cost, backward pass updates weights.
This cycle defines neural network training.
animations: Highlight prediction, error calculation, and update stages.
Animate the loop repeating to illustrate convergence.
